stories.name: Telangana plans global logistics hub by 2047
stories.summary: Telangana has laid out a structured roadmap to become a global logistics hub by 2047, emphasizing infrastructure expansion, digital integration, AI-enabled logistics, sustainability and skills development, with projects including a Regional Ring Road, Metro Rail Phase II, proposed airports, a dry port, Logistics Policy 2.0 and dedicated logistics parks. Chief Minister Revanth Reddy is concurrently pushing a manufacturing-growth agenda to attract global investment, leverage emerging technologies such as AI, and prioritize skilling and reskilling to boost jobs and industrial output. These state-level plans align with a broader national industrial and warehousing boom spurred by policy initiatives like PM Gati Shakti, the National Logistics Policy and multimodal logistics parks, with a recent report identifying 30 high-potential cities and rising demand for Grade A facilities. However, Telangana faces fiscal pressures at home after successive pay revisions that have sharply raised salary and pension bills in power utilities, complicating funding for subsidies and infrastructure without increased borrowing. At the same time, India’s localization-linked incentives for batteries, autos and electric vehicles have drawn international scrutiny and prompted the WTO to establish a panel at China’s request, posing potential trade and policy risks for the country’s industrial strategy.
keyPoints: Under the Telangana Rising 2047 framework the state aims to raise its share of India’s GDP from about 5% to 10% by 2047 and build a USD 3‑trillion state economy.
The Telangana government is working with Young India Skills University and industry partners to develop a skilled workforce tailored to emerging logistics requirements.

Successive pay revisions have produced sharp wage increases in the power sector: senior sweepers are reported earning up to Rs 200,000 per month, overall salary and pension expenditures have risen to about Rs 6,000 crore, and Telangana Power Generation Corporation’s monthly salary bill is around Rs 300 crore.

stories.name: Adobe launches Firefly Quick Cut, auto-assembles rough edits
stories.summary: Adobe’s Firefly has a new Quick Cut feature that turns uploaded or AI-generated footage into a structured first cut from plain-language prompts, with optional scripts or shot lists to guide the assembly. The tool automatically selects takes, trims filler, inserts transitions (and can even generate brief transition shots from frames), and lets users set aspect ratio, pacing, duration, and optional B-roll while producing an editable timeline rather than a locked render. Firefly combines models from Adobe, Google, OpenAI, and Runway in a single app and Adobe is offering unlimited image and video generations up to 2K on select plans through March 16. Adobe frames Quick Cut as a way to eliminate grunt work and give creators a clear starting point while preserving creative control. Creators such as Brandon Baum and Sophia Kianni praise Firefly for speeding ideation and providing multiasset support for small businesses, podcasters, and marketers. Adobe positions Quick Cut as useful for both whole-project assembly edits and localized fixes, helping product reviewers, reporters, podcasters, and marketers iterate faster.
keyPoints: YouTuber Brandon Baum said he uses Firefly as a “thought starter,” adding: “I like to generate a few things, iterate on my ideas quickly, try, try, try, fail fast, and hopefully find the gold.”

Adobe product lead Mike Polner framed Quick Cut around speed and iteration: “When inspiration strikes, video creators need tools that keep pace with the speed of their minds... They need to fill their timeline quickly, so they can build on top of it and when necessary, tear it down and build anew.”

The March 16 promotion applies to specific Firefly plans (Firefly Pro, Firefly Premium, and 4,000‑, 7,000‑, and 50,000‑credit plans) and includes unlimited generations with several image models named by Adobe: Google Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image Generation, Runway Gen‑4 Image, as well as Adobe’s own Firefly image and video models.

stories.name: Adobe Stock Drops 42% After Target Cuts
stories.summary: Adobe shares have fallen sharply this year after a run of analyst price-target cuts — including Jefferies’ reduction to $290 — leaving the stock trading roughly in the $246–$255 range in late February. The pullback reflects broader tech weakness and investor concern about AI-driven competition (including new image-editing features from Google) and has produced roughly 23% year-to-date and about 43% one-year declines. Still, valuation metrics look relatively attractive: Simply Wall St scores Adobe 5 out of 6 on valuation checks, and the company shows strong free cash flow and a forward P/E near 15. Adobe reported record 2025 revenue of $23.77 billion (about 11% year-over-year) and continues to push AI-powered creative and marketing tools. Analysts remain divided — some see multi-year downside with targets implying levels near $200 by 2030 while others view the pullback as a buying opportunity — leaving Adobe as a fundamentally profitable but competitively pressured tech leader.
keyPoints: Simply Wall St cites Adobe's latest twelve‑month free cash flow at about $9.77 billion and uses a 2‑stage Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE) DCF model that projects Adobe's free cash flow rising to roughly $13.02 billion by 2030.

Other recent analyst moves beyond Jefferies' cut: HSBC trimmed its price target to $302 from $388 on Feb. 13, and Piper Sandler downgraded Adobe to Neutral and lowered its price target to $330 (from $470).

Despite the negative sentiment and price‑target reductions, Adobe was listed among the '10 Best Magic Formula Stocks for 2026' and was described as having a 'Moderate Buy' rating with an average upside potential of about 70.9% as of Feb. 23.

stories.name: WPP, Adobe deepen global AI marketing partnership
stories.summary: On Feb. 24, 2026 WPP and Adobe deepened their global partnership to deliver a unified, AI-driven marketing solution by embedding Adobe Firefly Foundry into WPP’s agentic marketing platform, WPP Open. The collaboration combines Adobe’s generative AI, content platforms and data orchestration with WPP’s strategic, creative and media expertise to automate planning, creation, production and activation through agentic workflows that generate and adapt content while optimizing media spend. Firefly Foundry enables brands to train models on cleared IP so generated content is brand-safe and suitable for commercial use, and the integrated approach is designed to be privacy-conscious across the marketing lifecycle. The partners say the move tackles the industry’s pressure to produce more personalized content across more channels by streamlining fragmented tools and multistep processes into a single flow that frees human teams for higher-level creativity. WPP and Adobe also plan investments in training creative AI engineers to help clients adopt AI-led marketing processes and ensure human oversight remains central.
keyPoints: WPP Open is already in wide internal use across the group — more than 85,000 WPP employees use the platform.

WPP CTO Stephan Pretorius: “For years, we’ve watched brilliant creative ideas get stuck in production queues… With Adobe, we’re shattering the barriers between ideation and impact, building agentic content systems that handle the complexity so human creativity can soar.”

Adobe says Firefly Foundry enables development of generative AI models that are 'responsibly trained' on a customer's cleared IP and can be 'approved for commercial deployment', a phrasing the partners use to emphasise legal/brand safety for generated content.

stories.name: Telangana CM, Adobe CEO Discuss Investments, AI Impact
stories.summary: On Feb. 25, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met Adobe CEO Shantanu Narayen, a member of the Telangana Rising 2047 vision board, to discuss a roadmap for positioning the state as a global manufacturing hub and attracting major firms. The two discussed global manufacturing trends, green energy and the impact of artificial intelligence on the economy, emphasizing the need for skilling and reskilling to address job disruption. Reddy urged more cooperation from Narayen and called for new, aggressive plans by the state government to secure large international investments. The meeting aligns with Reddy’s broader push—outlined at the India AI Summit—for a national assessment of AI-driven job displacement and significant investment in workforce retraining.
keyPoints: The meeting was held at Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s official residence in Jubilee Hills.
Shantanu Narayen’s visit was described as a courtesy call on the Chief Minister.
Details of the interaction were released through an official government release, which summarised the topics discussed and the need for a roadmap to attract investments.

stories.name: Major funds raise Adobe holdings
stories.summary: Multiple institutional investors raised stakes in Adobe Inc. according to recent Form 13F filings, with Vanguard Mega Cap Index Fund adding 8,837 shares to hold about 88,149 shares (~$28.2M) and Vanguard S&P 500 Growth Index Fund adding 2,710 shares to hold about 120,876 shares (~$38.7M). Eagle Global Advisors increased its position by 1,010 shares to 1,988 shares (about $695,780), while other firms including Leelyn Smith, Salomon & Ludwin and Allen Mooney & Barnes also reported meaningful increases (Allen Mooney & Barnes added 32,864 shares to hold 38,403 shares, per filings). The coverage highlights a broad institutional buying trend across both large index funds and smaller advisors. Reported market-market details show Adobe trading in the mid-$250s with a 52-week low near $251 and reported highs in the mid-$400s, a market capitalization around $106 billion and a price-to-earnings ratio near 15.5.
keyPoints: Allen Mooney & Barnes Investment Advisors LLC boosted its Adobe stake by 593.32%, purchasing 32,864 shares to bring its total to 38,403 shares valued at about $13,440,670.
Capital Group Growth ETF bought 31,632 shares of Adobe, raising its position to 246,352 shares worth approximately $78,864,670.
Sparkline Intangible Value ETF initiated a new position in Adobe, purchasing 1,142 shares valued at roughly $365,590.

stories.name: Adobe announces free creative tools for Indian students
stories.summary: Adobe announced a program giving students in accredited Indian higher-education institutions free access to flagship tools including Photoshop, Acrobat and Firefly, with access routed through participating colleges and institutions rather than direct public sign-up. The offering includes AI-first learning modules, structured curriculum and guided training, plus industry-recognized certifications through a partnership with NASSCOM FutureSkills Prime supported by MeitY. Adobe said the move is intended to boost AI skills and the country’s creator economy while aligning with the government’s digital-skill and 'Create in India' priorities. The initiative also plans to extend to thousands of schools and hundreds of colleges establishing Content Creator Labs to support practical learning. Company chair and CEO Shantanu Narayen framed the effort as empowering students with AI capabilities to help advance the nation’s development goals.
keyPoints: Adobe announced the programme at the AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi.
Some reports describe the announcement as having been made in Chandigarh, indicating differing accounts of the event location in media coverage.
Adobe said this new offering extends its existing Digital Academy programme in India through the NASSCOM FutureSkills Prime partnership.

stories.name: Adobe Faces AI-Training Lawsuits, Analyst Downgrades
stories.summary: Adobe shares have plunged roughly 43% over the past year and now trade near $264 as investors reassess large software names and several firms (Goldman Sachs, UBS, Piper Sandler) have downgraded the stock, citing weaker near-term revenue and EPS versus peers. The company now faces renewed legal pressure from lawsuits alleging it used pirated books to train its AI models—new suits in February follow a December filing—which raises regulatory, reputational and financial risk for its AI roadmap. At the same time Adobe is pushing an enterprise AI strategy, announcing an AI-focused collaboration with Cognizant and promoting Firefly/GenStudio and Acrobat AI Assistant as monetization levers aimed at scaled content supply chains. Valuation views diverge sharply: a Simply Wall St. DCF implies a much higher intrinsic value (around $545 per share), while analysts cutting ratings highlight near-term execution risk and competition from AI-native rivals. The near-term investor debate centers on whether Adobe can translate its AI products into sustainable revenue and pricing power without legal setbacks eroding its creative and document franchises.
keyPoints: TV host Jim Cramer criticized Adobe’s positioning in the AI market, saying, "Well Adobe’s been cut in half. And I think Adobe, you can very quickly disable the 660 dollar Adobe [inaudible] that I have. I don’t need it anymore. I got the same thing going for 60 bucks. So that’s in trouble, that’s trouble."

A Bloomberg-reported lawsuit filed Feb. 9 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California alleges Adobe willfully used pirated books to train its AI models and cites infringement of hundreds of thousands of books.

Adobe’s published growth narrative projects $29.3 billion in revenue and $8.7 billion in earnings by 2028, implying roughly 9.0% annual revenue growth and about a $1.8 billion increase in earnings from $6.9 billion today — assumptions investors must accept for the bullish case.

stories.name: Canva Hits $4B ARR, AI Fuels Growth
stories.summary: Canva closed 2025 with about $4 billion in annual recurring revenue as monthly active users rose roughly 20% to ~265 million and paid subscribers exceeded 31 million, growth company leaders attribute largely to new AI features. The company doubled its B2B ARR to $500 million while remaining skewed to North America and pursuing lower-priced subscriptions in markets like Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica to expand monetization. Management is repositioning Canva as an AI-first platform—a “design agency in your pocket”—anchored by tools such as Magic Write/Magic Design and an AI mini-app/website generator that has over 10 million monthly users. Deepening integrations with large language models and chatbots (including ChatGPT and Claude) produced millions of in-chat interactions (26M+ by October 2025) and rising double-digit LLM-driven referral traffic, creating a new low-cost discovery channel. The results validate Canva’s AI pivot and sharpen competition with legacy creative software vendors as LLMs emerge as a major distribution gateway.
keyPoints: Canva’s co-founder and COO Cliff Obrecht said the company is “inverting” its strategy—moving from a design platform with AI tools to an AI platform with design tools, calling Canva more like a “cursor for design.”

Canva is actively dedicating resources to appear in LLM-driven search results and is investing in SEO and content around user search intents because it sees ChatGPT and other LLMs as the new top-of-funnel for user acquisition.

Canva faces named competition from established players including Adobe and Freepik as well as Apple, which is pushing a bundled Creator Studio (apps like Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor and MainStage) as a rival creative offering.

stories.name: 51 AVGC-XR startups expected at WAVES Corner
stories.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurated the WAVES Creators Corner at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, highlighting the growing use of AI in creative content and noting India has onboarded more than 38,000 high-end GPUs (with plans to add more), subsidized access and large AI investment commitments tied to the summit. The WAVES Creators Corner, powered by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and facilitated by WaveX, brings 51 AVGC-XR and media-tech startups to the India AI Impact Expo to showcase AI-driven animation pipelines, real-time rendering, immersive XR, virtual production, gaming and content-monetization technologies. Demonstrations include a Zero-Touch Autonomous Newsroom that converts live feeds into multilingual breaking news, the Bhasha-Wall offering real-time lip-synced dubbing across multiple Indian languages alongside an AI sign-language avatar, and immersive exhibits such as Samvad Setu, The Director’s Chair, an AI podcast studio, conversational humanoid robots and voice cloning. The pavilion pairs these showcases with panels, masterclasses and industry collaborations — including Adobe’s Kathavatar and a masterclass by Shekhar Kapur — to discuss responsible AI, cultural authenticity and tools for preserving linguistic and cultural heritage. Overall, the showcase aims to position India as a leader in responsible creative AI by connecting startups, investors, policymakers and global stakeholders and shifting focus from foundational compute to India-specific design, R&D and productization.
keyPoints: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw singled out Kuku’s platform at the event, saying, “AI is being used very effectively in the world of creative content... you should definitely check out Kuku’s platform. It has immense potential.”

Under the IndiaAI Mission India has onboarded more than 38,000 high‑end GPUs and is expected to add another 20,000; these GPUs are available at about Rs 65 per hour — roughly one‑third of the global average cost.

Vaishnaw indicated AI‑related investments tied to the summit are likely to exceed USD 200 billion, with about USD 90 billion already committed, and that the government is in talks with several large companies on further AI infrastructure investments.

stories.name: Photoshop adds Clarity, Dehaze, Grain adjustment layers
stories.summary: Adobe’s latest Photoshop release brings Clarity, Dehaze and Grain into the program as full, non‑destructive adjustment layers—maskable, stackable and blendable—so photographers can apply and revisit those Camera Raw effects without Smart Objects, layer duplication or complex modal workflows. The change makes common tasks simpler (for example, applying Dehaze only to distant elements, varying Grain across an image, or targeting Clarity to eyes or textures) and preserves image quality while allowing opacity and blend‑mode experimentation. Adobe also upgraded its Firefly‑powered Generative Fill, Generative Expand and Remove tools to produce higher‑quality 2K output with improved prompt adherence and fewer artifacts, and improved Reference Image handling to better preserve object identity with geometry‑aware scale, rotation and perspective. Photoshop adds other workflow refinements—including a beta Dynamic Text feature for one‑click circular/curved text paths—and Adobe says the updates are intended to reduce tedious steps so creatives can iterate faster. Overall, the suite of changes aims to give photographers and visual artists more precise, geometry‑aware control and faster, less frictional editing inside Photoshop.
keyPoints: The Grain adjustment layer exposes three separate sliders — Amount, Size and Roughness — letting users control not just strength but the look and scale of the grain; authors recommend applying grain after finishing other edits and sizing it to the output dimensions.

Photoshop combines Clarity and Dehaze into a single adjustment layer (rather than two wholly separate layers), so those two effects are delivered together as a maskable, blend-mode–compatible adjustment.

The release is Photoshop version 27.2; Adobe’s Pam Clark (product manager for Photoshop) framed the update as aimed at reducing friction for fast-moving creative professionals: “If you’re a creative professional, you move fast, chasing an idea from first spark to final pixel, and the smallest amount of friction can slow your creative output.”

stories.name: Apple launches Creator Studio subscription bundle
stories.summary: Apple launched Apple Creator Studio on Jan. 28, a subscription bundle that brings Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro (plus Motion, Compressor and MainStage) together across Mac, iPad and iPhone with pricing at $12.99/month or $129/year (discounted student/educator plans and a one-month free trial are available). The bundle includes Pixelmator Pro — an app Apple recently acquired — arriving on iPad with a touch-optimized interface and Apple Pencil support. Apple is rolling new “intelligent” on-device features across the suite: Final Cut Pro adds transcript/visual search, beat detection and improved iPad exporter behavior, Logic Pro gains Chord ID and Synth Player tools, and Keynote/Pages/Numbers get premium templates and a Content Hub. On iPad some apps are now subscription-only while Mac versions remain available as one-time purchases, and Apple emphasizes privacy, family sharing and education pricing to lower the barrier for creators. Early hands-on impressions call the bundle a strong value that should spur continued investment in these pro apps, though reviewers acknowledge subscription fatigue for some users.
keyPoints: Final Cut Pro ships as version 12 and the iPad app gains several practical workflow improvements beyond basic export fixes — multi-selection for batch adjustments, external-monitor preview support, and use of iPadOS 26’s background API so exports can continue while you leave the app.
Keynote’s new intelligence features can generate a first draft of a presentation from a simple text outline and can also create presenter notes automatically from existing slides.

Apple Creator Studio is part of a broader push to grow Apple’s services business into professional software — Apple’s services brought in tens of billions of dollars and 2025 was a record year, and this bundle extends that strategy into pro creative tools.

stories.name: Adobe Shares Fall 3.6%, Short Interest Rises
stories.summary: Shares of Adobe Inc. fell about 3.6% in mid‑day trading on Jan. 27 to roughly $293.85, trading just above its 52‑week low and well below its 52‑week high on below‑average volume. Analysts’ one‑year average price target is $425.27—implying roughly 45% upside—and the consensus brokerage rating is 2.3 (“Outperform”), while GuruFocus’s GF Value projects an even larger fair‑value upside. Short interest has risen 6.86% to 12.37 million shares, equal to 2.96% of float (about 3.8 days to cover), which remains below the peer‑group short‑interest average of 4.46%. Institutional activity is mixed: GF Fund Management and several advisors raised stakes and BCS Wealth initiated a new position, while Vanguard Personalized Indexing trimmed its holding by about 10%. The stock trades with a market capitalization near $123.6 billion and a P/E around 18, with recent 50‑ and 200‑day moving averages in the low‑to‑mid $300s, providing valuation context for the divergent analyst and investor signals.
keyPoints: GuruFocus's one‑year GF Value for Adobe is $668.90 — implying a 127.63% upside from the current price — and GF Value is calculated from the stock’s historical multiples, past growth and future estimates.
On Jan. 27 the stock hit an intraday low of $293.13 and trading volume was 1,359,590 shares, roughly 30.3% of the average daily volume of 4,483,880, indicating below‑average turnover.
GF Fund Management Co. Ltd. increased its Adobe holding by 23.79%, buying 20,243 shares to hold 105,329 shares valued at about $36,864,100 in the most recent 13F filing.

stories.name: Adobe adds AI PDF podcast, slide generation
stories.summary: Adobe rolled out generative-AI features across Acrobat, Acrobat Studio and Adobe Express that turn PDFs into interactive resources, including podcast-style audio summaries, slide-deck generation and chat-style prompt editing. The Generate Presentation feature creates an outline from files in PDF Spaces and then produces editable slide decks using Adobe Express themes, stock images, brand assets and animations. The Generate Podcast produces podcast-style spoken overviews (Adobe defaults to a two-host conversation) and currently uses Microsoft GPT for transcription and a Google voice model while Adobe continues testing models. Acrobat’s AI Assistant supports prompt-driven edits—removing pages, replacing text, inserting comments, adding e-signatures, setting passwords—and embeds AI summaries with citations pointing to exact locations in source files. Adobe says the updates build on Acrobat Studio and earlier ChatGPT/Firefly integrations, rely on generative AI trained on commercially licensed data, and have driven improved efficiency and user growth.
keyPoints: Adobe cited a Forrester TEI study and internal metrics showing Acrobat’s AI usage has grown fourfold, the AI agent improved document summarization and analysis efficiency by about 45%, and monthly active users of Acrobat and Adobe Express grew ~20% year‑over‑year.

Although Generate Podcast currently uses a Microsoft GPT model for transcription and a Google voice model for audio, Adobe also has its own audio AI model and says it may swap or add models as it continues testing.

Generate Presentation can draw from a very large template library — Adobe Express offers access to over 500,000 professional templates — and lets users apply brand themes, stock images, and animations from Express to the auto‑generated decks.

stories.name: Adobe Unveils Firefly Foundry, Partners Hollywood Studios
stories.summary: Adobe unveiled Firefly Foundry at the start of the Sundance Film Festival, announcing partnerships with major talent agencies, studios, VFX firms, directors and film schools—including CAA, UTA, WME, B5 Studios, Promise Advanced Imagination, Cantina Creative, David Ayer, Jaume Collet-Serra and Parsons—to bring brand-specific generative AI into media and entertainment workflows. Firefly Foundry lets organizations collaborate directly with Adobe engineers to tune Firefly models on proprietary brand or franchise content, producing high-fidelity images, video, audio, 3D and vector outputs across pre-production, on-set iteration and post-production. Adobe frames Foundry as “commercially safe” and ethically trained to preserve authorship, ownership and creative control while enabling faster scaling of short-form, immersive and marketing content, and cites long-standing industry usage of its tools. Partners say the platform can accelerate ideation and production and help smaller indie shops, but the rollout also revives industry concerns about rights, provenance and the potential impact on creative workers, prompting emphasis on governance, licensing and protections.
keyPoints: Justin Hackney, co-founder and CCO of Wonder Studio, said of the partnership: “Our mission is to protect the soul of the work as tools evolve,” arguing that partnering with Adobe removes friction between imagination and execution and unlocks new visual languages.
Adobe claims that its tools were used on 85% of the films premiering at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, a statistic it cites to underscore its longstanding footprint in film production.
Several well-known brands are already using Firefly Foundry for media production, including The Home Depot, HUMAIN and Walt Disney Imagineering.

stories.name: Controllers Council projects subscription economy $650B-$1.5T
stories.summary: Recurring revenue is income businesses receive at regular intervals—typically from subscriptions, memberships, service contracts or other periodic charges—providing more predictable cash flow than one‑time purchases. That predictability changes operations: subscription businesses can forecast, hire, and invest differently and more confidently than firms reliant on one‑off sales. Controllers Council data cited in the reporting projects the global subscription economy will grow from about $650 billion in 2023 to over $1.5 trillion by 2027, and firms that build recurring streams often grow five to 10 times faster than traditional sellers. For startups, recurring revenue offers stability, deeper customer relationships that compound over time, and clearer data for planning and scaling. Finance teams and founders therefore focus on choosing the right recurring model, tracking key metrics, and navigating implementation and retention challenges; Brex’s guide walks through these definitions, model choices, metrics to monitor, and practical steps.
keyPoints: The articles use concrete industry examples to illustrate recurring revenue: a media company with paying subscribers or a SaaS business with monthly fees operate in the recurring‑revenue world, while a retail shop relying solely on walk‑in customers does not.

One vivid comparison contrasts two software firms: a company selling perpetual licenses must 'start from scratch every quarter' to meet targets, whereas a subscription firm 'wakes up on the first of the month knowing that a significant portion of its revenue is already secured.'
The reporting frames recurring revenue as the metric 'modern businesses obsess over' and insists the growth statistics are 'not marketing fluff' but 'the math of predictability.'

stories.name: Adobe launches Premiere 26 with AI-powered Object Mask
stories.summary: Adobe launched Premiere 26 alongside After Effects 26, introducing an AI-powered Object Mask that lets editors hover and click to generate and automatically track precise masks, dramatically reducing manual rotoscoping. The masking tools — including redesigned Shape Masks — use Adobe’s on-device AI model so all processing and footage remain local, boosting tracking performance up to roughly 20× and avoiding cloud latency and data-training concerns. Premiere 26 adds tighter integrations with Adobe Stock and Firefly Boards to streamline media import, while After Effects 26 includes SVG import and new 3D parametric mesh and motion-design features. Adobe timed the release to coincide with Sundance, where its tools are used on a large share of festival films, and demonstrated workflows like isolating subjects for color grading or effects. Company notes and reviewers caution that AI masks can still need manual refinement for fast-moving subjects or complex occlusions, but for typical tasks the feature promises substantial time savings for editors.
keyPoints: Adobe removed the “Pro” suffix from the product name — the new release is called Adobe Premiere 26 (dropping the “Pro” suffix).
Adobe says 85% of the films premiering at the Sundance Film Festival this year were edited with Adobe Creative Cloud tools — a key reason the company timed the release to coincide with Sundance.

Object Mask’s UI offers multiple overlay preview options (six colored overlays or a black-and-white alpha view) and built-in quick-edit tools — you can add/subtract mask areas with fast lasso and rectangular tools and adjust feathering and resizing directly from the toolbar.

stories.name: Adobe appoints Airbnb tech veteran Lucius DiPhillips CIO
stories.summary: Adobe has named Lucius DiPhillips its new chief information officer to lead the company’s global Technology Services team as it scales AI-driven innovation and digital transformation. DiPhillips joins with more than 25 years of technology leadership, most recently serving as CIO at Airbnb, and will focus on modernizing enterprise architecture, strengthening core systems, and improving employee and customer experiences. His background includes senior technology roles across firms such as eBay, PayPal, Bank of America, GE, Workday and Oracle, where he delivered infrastructure savings, operational improvements and introduced AI-enhanced capabilities. Adobe executives, including CFO Daniel Durn, praised his people-first leadership and vision as instrumental for scaling AI, and DiPhillips said Adobe’s focus on AI and trust was a key reason for taking the role. The hire comes as Adobe accelerates deployment of AI tools across products and internal processes, increasing demands on its technology foundation.
keyPoints: Adobe announced the hire on January 20, 2026, and DiPhillips replaces Cynthia Stoddard, who left Adobe last year to become CIO at Intel Corp.
At Airbnb, DiPhillips implemented AI-enhanced security and analytics that improved the company’s operational resilience during periods of surging demand.
Following DiPhillips’s departure from Airbnb, the company appointed Ahmad Al-Dahle as its Chief Technology Officer.

stories.name: Adobe announces $10M fund for underrepresented creators
stories.summary: At the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, Adobe announced it will commit $10 million in grants and donated products through its Film & TV Fund to expand access and career advancement for underrepresented creators. Launched in 2024 and having supported more than 1,000 creators, the fund now adds a direct-to-creators pathway alongside community partner nominations, with participating organizations including Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively’s Group Effort Initiative, USC Annenberg, the NAACP and Gold House. Adobe is partnering with Dimz Inc. Academy and Rideback RISE and is expanding support for Sundance Ignite with a new short-film fund to help alumni take projects from concept to screen. In parallel, Adobe is shipping AI-powered updates to Premiere and After Effects—such as Firefly Boards integration (using Adobe and third-party models from Google, OpenAI and Runway), faster masking and object selection tools, native 3D parametric meshes in After Effects, and an Adobe Stock panel—to speed postproduction workflows. Application details will be released later this year, and interested filmmakers can sign up for updates via createchange@adobe.com.
keyPoints: Adobe said a Sundance Institute survey found roughly 85% of films at the festival used Adobe products, underscoring the company’s deep penetration in indie filmmaking workflows.
The new Adobe Stock panel inside Premiere lets editors browse, preview, license and import from a catalogue of more than 52 million clips without leaving the application.

The After Effects update includes additions beyond native 3D parametric meshes — such as new spot and parallel shadow controls and more than 1,300 free Substance 3D materials users can apply to designs.

stories.name: Software Stocks Drop After Anthropic Claude Code Update
stories.summary: Software and SaaS stocks plunged as investors reacted to Anthropic’s Claude updates — including a recent Claude Code capability that can automate workflows and coding — stoking fears about displacement of traditional application revenue. Salesforce in particular fell into technical "oversold" territory with an RSI near 29 and traded around $225.93 on Jan. 20–21, marking an eight-day losing streak, roughly a 15% drop over that stretch and declines of about 31%–39% from 52‑week/all‑time highs. The weakness is part of a broader rout in large software names, with a Morgan Stanley–tracked basket of SaaS stocks down about 15% so far in 2026 after an 11% decline in 2025 and steep weekly losses at firms such as Intuit and Adobe. Analysts say the speed of agentic AI improvements makes forecasting growth difficult and raises questions about incumbents' per-seat subscription economics and ability to monetize or incorporate these new capabilities.
keyPoints: Anthropic’s recent release that stoked the selloff was rolled out on Jan. 12 — the update to its Claude agent rekindled disruption fears across software makers.

Claude Code functions as a fully autonomous, command-line style system that can integrate developer workflows end-to-end — writing, testing and debugging complete software stacks with minimal human oversight.

Several large software names are among the S&P 500’s worst performers YTD — CNBC named Intuit, ServiceNow, GoDaddy, AppLovin and Adobe as the worst performers (in that order) — and Intuit tumbled about 16% in a week, its worst drop since 2022.

stories.name: Reports: Savory ice cream gains mainstream traction
stories.summary: Ice cream is showing up in diverse headlines this week — from a Times Now optical-illusion brain teaser that asks readers to spot a hidden cone in a crowded holiday market to food coverage tracing century-old traditions like Grape‑Nuts cereal ice cream and its regional popularity. Culinary reporting also finds savory ice creams moving from gimmick to trend, with chefs and shops experimenting with ingredients such as miso, balsamic, Parmesan served alongside salmorejo, and olive oil or soy sauce toppings. On the business front, Bloomberg reports Unilever is carving out its Magnum brand, with the company’s CFO outlining plans to boost capital spending and accelerate growth in 2026. Together the pieces illustrate ice cream’s reach across viral culture, evolving flavor innovation, and corporate strategy.
keyPoints: Ice‑cream innovator Van Leeuwen rolled out several of the early savory/novelty flavors that helped popularize the trend: mac and cheese in 2021, a pizza flavor in 2022 (which included basil cookies and a tomato jam swirl), and a ranch ice cream in 2023.

Smaller shops are experimenting too — The Outside Scoop blends roasted cherries and goat cheese, while shops like Clementine’s Ice Cream (St. Louis) and Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams (Columbus) have offered flavors featuring ingredients such as balsamic vinegar, miso, bay leaf and white pepper.

At the bistro Torres y Garcia in Seville, the author encountered salmorejo served with Parmesan ice cream and crispy ham — an example cited as proof the savory‑ice‑cream idea has moved from gimmick to a thoughtful culinary pairing.

stories.name: Boxing Day Sparks Surge in Car Listings
stories.summary: The days after Christmas are a peak moment for both bargain-hunters and people offloading unwanted items: Motorway CEO Tom Leathes says Boxing Day and the days after see a sharp rise in private used‑car listings as owners act on New Year plans. Motorway’s app marketplace connects private sellers directly with dealers, typically earning sellers about £1,600 more than a part‑exchange and allowing smaller dealers to snap up stock while larger competitors are often shut. Retailers are also clearing inventory with steep end‑of‑year and New Year discounts across tech, home goods, mattresses and more, with some promotional ranges advertised up to around 80% off. The day after Christmas is an especially good time to buy discounted holiday décor, though shoppers should be selective to avoid poor-value purchases. Combined, these post‑holiday patterns create opportunities for sellers to monetize items quickly and for buyers to find significant deals.
keyPoints: Motorway sells up to around 2,000 cars a day and has boosted growth with high-profile marketing campaigns, including sponsorship of the Six Nations rugby competition.
The Motorway transaction process is fully handled via its app and includes the dealer collecting the car from the owner’s home once a sale is agreed; the company was founded in 2016.

Specific end-of-year discounts advertised include Amazon (up to ~40% off), Crate & Barrel (up to ~60% off), Nolah mattresses (35% off), Helix Sleep (up to 25% off plus a free sleep bundle), and NYDJ (up to ~80% off sitewide with promo code BYE25).

stories.name: Citi raises Adobe price target to $387
stories.summary: Baird raised its price target on Amplitude to $15 from $14 and maintained an Outperform rating after updating its model following meetings with management. Citi raised its price target on Adobe to $387 from $366 and kept a Neutral rating after a fiscal Q4 that beat estimates, though the firm called the fiscal 2026 outlook mixed. Other analysts differ on Adobe’s trajectory, with some (like Stifel) holding Buy views and high targets while firms such as Piper Sandler and Barclays trimmed prior targets amid concerns about moderating growth and competition; Adobe’s Q4 showed roughly $6.19 billion in revenue and stronger-than-expected non-GAAP EPS. Morgan Stanley raised its Apple price target to $315 from $305, kept an Overweight rating, and advised overweighting product-cycle beneficiaries like Apple and cloud-capex winners while being cautious on memory-exposed hardware names.
keyPoints: Adobe’s fiscal Q4 non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $5.50 and revenue was $6.19 billion, a roughly 10% year-over-year increase, with Adobe’s Digital Media segment (including Creative Cloud) contributing significantly to the gain.
Adobe shares dipped about 0.35% after the Q4 report, closing at $344.32 as investors digested the results and the mixed fiscal 2026 outlook.
Stifel reiterated a Buy rating on Adobe with a $450 price target, citing strong top-line performance and guidance — noting Adobe’s projected total ending ARR growth of more than 10%.

stories.name: Leica releases firmware 4.0 for SL3, Q3
stories.summary: Leica has released firmware 4.0.0 for the SL‑System (SL3 and SL3‑S) and the Q3 family (Q3, Q3 43 and Q3 Monochrom), delivering a suite of imaging, video and UI improvements. Key additions include direct Camera‑to‑Cloud connectivity with Adobe Frame.io, 3:2 and 4:3 open‑gate recording, expanded anamorphic support with in‑camera de‑squeeze, and additional video format options. AI‑assisted autofocus and a revised tracking algorithm improve detection and subject stability for human eyes/faces/bodies and a wide range of animals, while AF menu options have been simplified and expanded. The SL3 gains a Multi‑Shot mode that combines exposures into roughly 241MP files, plus faster startup, more stable S‑lens AF behavior, monitor refresh rate choices and battery health reporting. The Q3 line receives an SL3‑inspired user interface overhaul with faster navigation and improved touch controls, and the update is available via the Leica FOTOS app or by SD‑card install.
keyPoints: The firmware adds in‑camera anamorphic de‑squeeze with explicit supported squeeze factors: 1.25, 1.3, 1.33, 1.5, 1.6, 1.65, 1.8, 1.85 and 2.0x.
The SL3/SL3‑S can record 5.8K (5824 × 4368) at up to 29.97p internally, but that mode is limited to 4:2:0 10‑bit encoding at 200 Mbps.
Monitor refresh rate now offers 30 fps or 60 fps; choosing 30 fps reduces Live View power consumption.

stories.name: Adobe plans Semrush buy, faces proposed class-action
stories.summary: Adobe heads into a holiday‑thinned trading week with shares near $355–358 following a strong Q4 FY2025 that delivered record quarterly revenue of $6.19 billion, FY revenue of $23.77 billion and ending ARR of about $25.2 billion, but the stock remains roughly 20% below its 2025 highs. Management says AI‑influenced ARR now represents more than one‑third of the business and is shifting reporting emphasis to ARR and customer‑group subscription revenue to track AI monetization. The company is pushing distribution of AI products — including ChatGPT integrations, Firefly video upgrades and a Runway partnership — and strategic moves such as the Semrush acquisition are being watched as potential catalysts. Offsetting those positives are investor concerns about the timing of AI monetization, near‑term margin pressure from heavy AI investment, and rising legal scrutiny over model training data that could generate headline risk. Given thin holiday liquidity, any fresh analyst notes, legal updates or adoption datapoints could produce outsized stock swings ahead of FY2026 execution and March 2026 earnings.
keyPoints: Adobe repurchased roughly 7.2 million shares in Q4 FY2025 and nearly 31 million shares over the full fiscal year.
Operating cash flow was $3.16 billion in Q4 FY2025 and about $10.03 billion for the full fiscal year.

Adobe’s FY2026 financial guidance included total revenue of $25.9 billion to $26.1 billion and non‑GAAP EPS of $23.30 to $23.50; Q1 FY2026 guidance was revenue of $6.25–6.30 billion and EPS of $5.85–5.90.

stories.name: Adobe Faces Class-Action Over Alleged AI Training
Adobe Firefly AI
stories.summary: Adobe has rolled out a major Firefly update that lets creators make precise, prompt-based edits to existing AI-generated video clips using natural-language commands rather than regenerating whole scenes. The update adds camera-motion references—upload a start frame plus a reference video so Firefly recreates pan, dolly, zoom or tilt movements—to reduce jitter and produce consistent cinematic shots. A public-beta Firefly Video Editor (browser-based) provides a lightweight assembly space with timeline and text-based editing to combine generated clips, audio and personal footage. Adobe is integrating third-party models—Runway’s Aleph for surgical edits, Topaz Astra for upscaling (1080p to 4K) and Black Forest Labs’ FLUX.2 for higher-resolution image generation and editing—across Firefly, Photoshop and soon Adobe Express. To encourage adoption the company is offering limited-time unlimited generations for subscribers, positioning the changes as a shift from “prompt roulette” toward iterative, controlled creative workflows.
keyPoints: Black Forest Labs’ FLUX.2 can generate and edit images up to 1 megapixel, offers advanced text rendering and supports up to four reference images; FLUX.2 is available immediately in Firefly’s Text to Image, Prompt to Edit and Firefly Boards, is in Photoshop desktop, and will arrive in Adobe Express in January.

Adobe is using Runway’s Aleph model to enable surgical, prompt-driven edits (examples given: “remove the person on the left side of the frame,” “change the sky to overcast,” or “zoom in slightly on the main subject”), with changes applied directly to the existing clip rather than requiring a full regeneration.

Adobe is running a limited-time promotion granting unlimited generations of Firefly’s video and image models to specific subscriber plans (Firefly Pro, Firefly Premium, 7,000-credit, and 50,000-credit plans) through January 15.
